answer_1.quote: We introduce the novel task of document-level targeted content transfer, defined as rewriting a document to obey a user-provided constraint resulting in some systematic alteration of the document's content.
datasets: 1,254,931 recipes from online recipe websites and existing datasets
answer_1.outputs: Rewritten recipes that adhere to dietary constraints

answer_2.quote: We use automatic metrics and human judgments to evaluate the rewritten recipes, measuring their overall quality, their fluency, their dietary constraint accuracy, and their ability to produce diverse outputs without straying too far from the source recipe.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human-based evaluation using a crowdsourcing platform on rewrites from the best-performing models based on automatic metrics.
answer_4.guideline: We ask 5 judges to rate each rewritten recipe on a scale of 1 to 5 on these criteria: a. Ingredient usage, b. Closeness to source, c. Dietary constraint, d. Overall quality. We also collect human judgments on head-to-head comparisons between models.
